STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.speaker: Other commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.claim: A different reported view says verses 53–59 were all revealed concerning Waḥshī.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r4.anchor: while others say that vv. 53–59 were all revealed in regard to it

STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.claim: The call to repent in verses 54–67 leads into the final extended contrast between the believers’ and disbelievers’ ends in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:39:intro/r12.anchor: This is followed by an exhortation to turn to God in repentance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.claim: Rather than despairing of God or seeking deities and intercessors, people should turn to the forgiving and merciful God in every circumstance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r4.anchor: losing hope in God and seeking other deities and intercessors is not the correct way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.claim: People should turn to God and believe in His revealed Book before He seizes them; later regret and a wish to believe will be too late.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p522/r5.anchor: before He seizes them, people should turn to Him and profess faith in this magnificent Book

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r4.claim: A reported story tells of an Israelite scholar who abandoned learning and sinned after Satan promised he could repent later; death came as he enjoyed his wealth, and he regretted his disobedience too late.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r4.anchor: روي أنه كان في بني إسرائيل عالم ترك علمه وفسق، أتاه إبليس فقال له: تمتع من الدنيا ثم تب، فأطاعه وأنفق ماله في الفجور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya parses أن تقول as a purpose clause, meaning repent so that the soul will not say this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r5.anchor: أن تقول: مفعول من أجله، فقدره ابن عطية: أي أنيبوا من أجل أن تقول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes أن تقول as expressing avoidance: lest the soul say this.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r7.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r7.claim: Al-Hawfi supplies the implied warning: We warned you lest the soul say this.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers several readings of indefinite نفس: some souls, many souls, one unusually defiant soul, or one facing immense punishment; the author prefers the first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r8.anchor: ونكر نفس لأنه أريد بها بعض الأنفس، وهي نفس الكافر، أو أريد الكثير، كما قال الأعشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r9.claim: Among the explanations for the indefinite soul, the author finds the first, meaning the disbeliever's soul, apparent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r9.anchor: قال هذه المحتملات الزمخشري، والظاهر الأول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r10.claim: Most readers substitute an alif for the first-person yā in يا حسرتا; Abu Ja'far has an additive-yā reading and also a form combining alif and yā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يا حسرتا، بإبدال ياء المتكلم ألفا، وأبو جعفر: يا حسرتا، بياء الإضافة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r11.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r11.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi allows حسرتا as a dual meaning regret upon regret, or two regrets over losing Paradise and entering the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p212/r11.anchor: وقال أبو الفضل الرازي في تصنيفه (كتاب اللوامح) : ولو ذهب إلى أنه أراد تثنية الحسرة مثل لبيك وسعديك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads يا حسرتاه with a silent pause-ha when stopping.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في الوقف: يا حسرتاه، بهاء السكت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r2.claim: Sibawayh explains calling regret or woe as summoning it to arrive because its time has come.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه: ومعنى نداء الحسرة والويل: هذا وقتك فاحضري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r3.claim: Janb literally means side, but attributing a bodily limb to God is impossible, so the phrase is metaphorical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r3.anchor: والجنب: الجانب، ومستحيل على الله الجارحة، فإضافة الجنب إليه مجاز.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r4.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r4.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi interpret God's side as His command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد، والسدي: في أمر الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets it as God's mention, meaning the Qur'an and acting upon it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: في ذكره، يعني القرآن والعمل به.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r6.claim: Another explanation is neglect of God's obedience, taking janb to mean direction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r6.anchor: وقيل: في جهة طاعته، والجنب: الجهة، وقال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r7.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses جنب for a side or direction, supporting the lexical gloss of janb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r7.anchor: وقال الشاعر: أفي جنب تكنى قطعتني ملامة ... سليمى لقد كانت ملامتها ثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r8.speaker: الراجز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r8.claim: The rajaz line الناس جنب والأمير جنب likewise witnesses the meaning side or party.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r8.anchor: وقال الراجز: الناس جنب والأمير جنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r9.claim: Common expressions use janb for someone's side or vicinity, and Sabiq al-Barbari's line uses it for the right owed to a lover.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r9.anchor: ثم قالوا: فرط في جنبه، يريدون حقه. قال سابق البربري: أما تتقين الله في جنب عاشق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r10.claim: The phrase is a metonymy: locating something in a person's place or domain attributes it to that person, as in the cited line about virtues in Ibn al-Hashraj's dome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r10.anchor: وهذا من باب الكناية، لأنك إذا أثبت الأمر في مكان الرجل وحيزه، فقد أثبته فيه. ألا ترى إلى قوله: إن السماحة والمروءة والندى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r11.claim: ما فرطت is a verbal noun phrase meaning my neglect of obedience to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r11.anchor: وما في ما فرطت مصدرية، أي على تفريطي في طاعة الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r12.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r12.claim: Qatadah says the sinner not only neglected obedience but also mocked its adherents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r12.anchor: قال قتادة: لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى سخر من أهلها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses وإن كنت لمن الساخرين as a circumstantial clause meaning the speaker neglected duty while mocking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومحل وإن كنت النصب على الحال، كأنه قال: فرطت وأنا ساخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r14.claim: The author instead reads the phrase as a separate report of the sinner's former state, not a circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r14.anchor: ويظهر أنه استئناف إخبار عن نفسه بما كان عليه في الدنيا، لا حال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the sinner's three statements retain their order—regret, excuse about guidance, then wish to return—and the reply answers the one requiring an answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8.anchor: وهو أنه حكى أقوال النفس على ترتيبها ونظمها، ثم أجاب من بينها عما اقتضى الجواب.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r1.claim: أن تقول is a purpose complement (مفعول من أجله).
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r1.anchor: أن تقول }: مفعول من أجله، فقدره الزمخشري كراهة أن تقول،

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies كراهة: the people should turn back lest they say this.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r2.anchor: فقدره الزمخشري كراهة أن تقول، وابن عطية:

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya connects the purpose directly to أنيبوا.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r3.anchor: وابن عطية: أنيبوا من أجل أن تقول. وأبو البقاء والحوفي:

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء والحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥawfī supply أنذرناكم مخافة, “We warned you lest you say …”.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r4.anchor: وأبو البقاء والحوفي: أنذرناكم مخافة أن تقول.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r5.claim: No omitted governing verb is needed, since أنيبوا is already present.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى إضمار هذا العامل مع وجود " أنيبوا " وإنما نكر نفسا

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r6.claim: نفسا is indefinite to convey multitude, not one solitary soul; an al-Aʿshā verse illustrates singular-for-plural usage.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r6.anchor: وإنما نكر نفسا لأنه أراد التكثير، كقول الأعشى:

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r7.claim: Alternatively, it may mean a distinct soul marked by extreme persistence in disbelief or terrible punishment.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد: نفسا متميزة من بين الأنفس باللجاج الشديد في الكفر أو بالعذاب العظيم.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r8.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r8.claim: The common reading has final alif replacing the possessive yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r8.anchor: العامة على الألف بدلا من ياء الإضافة. وعن ابن كثير

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r9.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr has يا حسرتاه with the pause hāʾ at a stop.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r9.anchor: وعن ابن كثير " يا حسرتاه " بهاء السكت وقفا، وأبو جعفر

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads يا حسرتي, retaining the original possessive form.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r10.anchor: وأبو جعفر " يا حسرتي " على الأصل. وعنه أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r11.claim: Abu Jaʿfar also has يا حسرتاي with both alif and yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r11.anchor: وعنه أيضا " يا حسرتاي " بالألف والياء. وفيها وجهان،

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r12.claim: One analysis of يا حسرتاي combines the substitute (alif) with the element it replaces.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r12.anchor: أحدهما: الجمع بين العوض والمعوض منه.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r13.claim: Another analysis treats it as the dual of حسرة annexed to the speaker’s yāʾ; the objection is that the expected form would be يا حسرتي by merging the two yāʾs.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r13.anchor: والثاني: أنه تثنية " حسرة " مضافة لياء المتكلم. واعترض على هذا: بأنه كان ينبغي أن يقال: يا حسرتي بإدغام ياء النصب في ياء الإضافة.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r14.claim: The form is defended by the dialect of al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb and others, as in رأيت الزيدان.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r14.anchor: وأجيب: بأنه يجوز أن يكون راعى لغة الحارث ابن كعب وغيرهم نحو: " رأيت الزيدان ".

SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r15.claim: Two further analyses make the alif replace the yāʾ with a yāʾ added after it, or insert the alif between the annexed elements; both are weak.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56/r15.anchor: وقيل: الألف بدل من الياء والياء بعدها مزيدة. وقيل: الألف مزيدة بين المتضايفين، وكلاهما ضعيف.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r1.claim: ما is a verbal noun, meaning “for my neglect”; an understood annexed noun makes the phrase “in the matter of obedience to God.”
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r1.anchor: " ما " مصدرية أي: على تفريطي. وثم مضاف أي: في جنب طاعة الله.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, جنب الله means the matter, direction, or side; جنب فلان and جانبه mean his direction or region.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r2.anchor: المراد به الأمر والجهة. يقال: هو في جنب فلان وجانبه، أي: جهته وناحيته.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r3.claim: An anonymous rajaz line and another poet use جنب for “side”; examples are الناس جنب and في جنب بكر.

SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r4.claim: The phrase broadens from “side” to “right”: فرط في جنبه means that one neglected His due; a verse uses في جنب عاشق.
SAMIN-DURR:39:56#2/r4.anchor: أما تتقين الله في جنب عاشق

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r2.claim: The vocative means “O my regret”; using the call particle conveys that the regret has fully seized the speaker and will not leave.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r2.anchor: أي يا ندما، وحرف النداء يدل على تمكن القصة

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r4.speaker: الفراء
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ permits يا حسرتاه with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r4.anchor: وزعم الفراء أنه يجوز يا حسرتاه على كذا وكذا بفتح الهاء

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r5.speaker: الفراء
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r5.claim: The transmitted forms also include يا حسرتاه with kasra or ḍamma on the hāʾ.

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r6.speaker: النحويون أجمعون
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r6.claim: The grammarians unanimously disallow retaining the hāʾ in connected speech.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r6.anchor: والنحويون أجمعون لا يجيزون أن تثبت هذه الها في الوصل

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r7.speaker: رجل من بني أسد
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adduces a line attributed to a man of Banū Asad, from Banū Fuqʿas, using يا رباه; Zajjāj says this citation is mistaken and irrelevant to the verse.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r7.anchor: وزعم أنه أنشده من بني فقعس رجل من بني أسد

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r8.claim: Zajjāj rejects the cited poetry as a useful proof: he does not know why it was cited, it was never a Qur’anic reading, and it does not explain this verse.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ولا أدري لم استشهد بهذا، ولم يقرأ به قط،

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r9.claim: The Kufans recite the second line with بجمار rather than بحمار; Zajjāj says neither poetic citation helps explain the verse.

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r10.claim: أن تقول means “for fear that a soul should say” or “to avoid a soul saying it”; follow the revelation beforehand to avoid the later remorse.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r10.anchor: خوف أن تقول نفس وكراهة أن تقول نفس.

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r11.claim: جنب الله means God’s command or path: the path of monotheism and affirming the Messenger’s prophethood to which the person was called.
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r11.anchor: معنى (على ما فرطت في جنب الله) في أمر الله،

ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r12.claim: The speaker means, “I was nothing but one of the mockers.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r12.anchor: أي وما كنت إلا من المستهزئين

ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n60/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n60/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n60/r1.claim: Unless context indicates otherwise, nafs means a human being; Asad therefore renders its associated pronouns as masculine despite the noun's feminine Arabic gender.
ASAD-NOTES:39:54#n60/r1.anchor: it signifies a "human being"; hence, the personal pronouns relating to this term (which is feminine in Arabic) are masculine in my rendering.

BUKHARI:2661/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2661/r1.speaker: عائشة
BUKHARI:2661/r1.claim: Aisha recounts the slander against her, her exoneration through Qur'an 24:11 onward, and Abu Bakr's renewed support for Mistah after 24:22; the report does not explain 39:56, and states no grading.
BUKHARI:2661/r1.anchor: عن عائشة ـ رضى الله عنها ـ زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال لها أهل الإفك ما قالوا، فبرأها الله منه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r9.claim: A governing noun (mudāf) is omitted before “an,” as in examples discussed in earlier sūrahs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r9.anchor: A governing noun ( mud@āf) is suppressed before the word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r10.claim: God has made these arrangements so the heedless will not regret their neglect at accountability: worldly pleasures distracted them from the Hereafter, and they mocked its reminders.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p567/r10.anchor: lured away by the absorbing pleasures of this world they continued to remain oblivious of the Hereafter

QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#1/r1.speaker: Cs|Prn
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#1/r1.claim: The pronominal-glide form expands the lament with an audible -āya possessive glide.
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#1/r1.anchor: Cs|Prn, mutawatir: Pronominal-glide reading expands the cry with -āya, adding an audible possessive glide

QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#2/r1.speaker: Cs
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#2/r1.claim: The pausal hāʾ form releases or doubles the lament at pause before returning to the standard cry.
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#2/r1.anchor: Cs, mutawatir: Pausal hāʾ reading doubles or releases the lament at pause

QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#3/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#3/r1.claim: The sukūn/glide variant closes the final sound and changes the pause texture while preserving the lament's sense.
QIRAAT-ER:39:56:5#3/r1.anchor: skn, mutawatir: Sukūn/glide reading closes the final sound, altering pause texture

IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r2.claim: Aisha's tears stopped when the Prophet addressed her; as her parents fell silent, she felt too insignificant to expect revelation about her and had only hoped for a dream or report clearing her.
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r2.anchor: ولكني قد كنت أرجو أن يرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في نومه شيئا يكذب به الله عني، لما يعلم من براءتي

IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r4.claim: Aisha remained confident of her innocence while her parents feared the worst; after revelation came, the Prophet told her that God had declared her innocent.
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r4.anchor: ويقول: أبشري يا عائشة، فقد أنزل الله براءتك

IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r5.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r5.claim: The Prophet publicly recited the revelation clearing Aisha and ordered the prescribed penalty for Mistah ibn Athatha, Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hamna bint Jahsh for spreading the slander.
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r5.anchor: ثم أمر بمسطح بن أثاثة، وحسان بن ثابت، وحمنة بنت جحش، وكانوا ممن أفصح بالفاحشة، فضربوا حدهم

MUSLIM:7021/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7021/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSLIM:7021/r1.claim: Aisha recounts the slander against her, led by Abdullah b. Ubayy: after a lost necklace left her behind, Ṣafwān escorted her back; the Prophet urged repentance if guilty, but God revealed her innocence in ten verses (24:11), echoing 39:56.
MUSLIM:7021/r1.anchor: عن حديث عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال لها أهل الإفك ما قالوا فبرأها الله مما قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r1.claim: Zamakhshari construes the clause as a purpose object, supplying a deleted word meaning aversion and an omitted governing verb indicated by the preceding warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r1.anchor: في موضع المفعول له بتقدير مضاف وقدره الزمخشري كراهة وهو منصوب بفعل محذوف يدل عليه ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r2.claim: Because he does not require subject identity for the governing verb, Al-Alusi allows anibū or ittabiʿū to govern the clause; construing the omitted noun as aversion is preferable to al-Hawfi's fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r2.anchor: وأيا ما كان فهذه الكراهة مقابل الرضا دون الإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r3.claim: The estimated aversion means the opposite of divine approval, not divine will, so this grammatical construction does not entail the Mu'tazilite doctrine of will.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r3.anchor: فهذه الكراهة مقابل الرضا دون الإرادة فلا اعتزال في تقديرها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r4.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r4.claim: Al-Hawfi instead estimates fear: the warning was given for fear that a soul might say this.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes anibū the governing verb and supplies neither aversion nor fear.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r6.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r6.claim: Some grammarians understand the construction as meaning lest a soul should say.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r6.anchor: وذهب بعض النحاة إلى أن التقدير لئلا تقول

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r7.claim: The indefinite soul may signal a multitude in context, as in al-A'sha's verse where one noble stands for crowds of supporters; alternatively it means some souls, which Abu Hayyan considers likelier and which suffices for a warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r7.anchor: وتنكير ( نفس ) للتكثير بقرينة المقام كما في قول الأعشى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers the partitive sense, since only some souls need be the speakers for the threat to apply to every soul that might be one of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتبعيض لأن القائل بعض الأنفس واستظهره أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r9.claim: A proposed honorific sense is one uniquely distinguished soul, stubborn to an extreme or facing immense punishment; Al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r9.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون للتعظيم أي نفس متميزة من الأنفس إما بلجاج شديد أو بعذاب عظيم وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r10.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r10.claim: The alif replaces the possessive yā': Sibawayh explains the cry as calling regret to come, since its time has arrived.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r10.anchor: بالألف بدل ياء الإضافة والمعنى كما قال سيبويه يا حسرتي احضري فهذا وقتك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the phrase in pause with hāʾ al-sakt, ya hasratah.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r12.claim: Abu Ja'far has a possessive-yā' reading and another transmission combining compensatory alif with yā'; Al-Alusi calls the combination impermissible except as an exceptional usage and analogy.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r13.claim: The author of al-Kashf prefers treating the form as an emphatic dual, like labbayk and sa'dayk, following a dialect that retains dual alif in every case.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r13.anchor: فالأوجه أن يكون ثني الحسرة مبالغة على نحو لبيك وسعديك وأقام بين ظهريهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r14.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r14.claim: Al-Razi allows a genuine dual in that dialect, referring to grief over missing paradise and entering the fire; Al-Alusi prefers the intensive reading because the sorrows of Judgment Day are many.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r14.anchor: وجوز أبو الفضل الرازي في كتابه اللوامح أن تكون التثنية على ظاهرها على تلك اللغة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r15.claim: The phrase means because of my neglect; على is causal, ما is a verbal noun, and tafrīt means falling short. The construction also occurs in 2:185.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r16.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r16.claim: Al-Raghib says janb literally names a bodily side and is borrowed for the side or direction adjoining it; here it figuratively means God's direction, with an omitted noun for obedience or His due, namely obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r16.anchor: أصل الجنب الجارحة ثم يستعار للناحية والجهة التي تليها كعادتهم في استعارة سائر الجوارح

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r17.claim: Neglecting the direction of obedience is a metonym for neglecting obedience itself; wasting the sphere entails wasting what it contains, making the inference especially forceful.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r17.anchor: والكلام على حذف مضاف أي في جنب طاعة الله أو في حقه تعالى أي ما يحق له سبحانه ويلزم وهو طاعته

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r18.speaker: سابق البربري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r18.claim: Al-Alusi cites Sabiq al-Barbari's line about a lover's right as poetic evidence for janb meaning a direction or due.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r18.anchor: وعلى ذلك قول سابق البربري من شعراء الحماسة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r19.speaker: زياد الأعجم
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r19.claim: Ziyad al-A'jam's verse about generosity, manliness, and liberality in a dome supplies an analogy for abstract qualities being assigned a place or direction.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r20.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r20.claim: Al-Imam explains janb as a side because necessary attendant matters resemble a limb or one of a thing's sides, allowing the word for a right, command, or obedience; he treats it as explicit metaphor without an omitted noun, a view Al-Alusi rejects.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r20.anchor: وقال الإمام : سمي الجنب لأنه جانب من جوانب الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as what the speaker neglected of God's reward.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r22.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r22.claim: Muqatil glosses it as what the speaker neglected of God's remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r22.anchor: ومقاتل : على ما ضيعت من ذكر الله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r23.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r23.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi understand it as neglecting God's command.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r23.anchor: ومجاهد والسدي : على ما فرطت في أمر الله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r24.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r24.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as neglecting obedience to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r25.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r25.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr glosses it as neglecting God's due.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r25.anchor: وسعيد بن جبير : في حق الله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r26.claim: A proposal takes janb figuratively as God's essence, like side or assembly; Al-Alusi rejects it as awkward and unsuitable to apply to God even metaphorically.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r26.anchor: الجنب مجاز على الذات كالجانب أو المجلس يستعمل مجازا لربه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r27.claim: Another proposal makes janb a metaphor for proximity to God; Al-Alusi rejects it because it requires another metaphor and ultimately reduces to obedience or its like.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r27.anchor: هو مجاز على القرب أي على ما فرطت في قرب الله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r28.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r28.claim: The phrase cannot be retained in its literal bodily sense, since God is transcendent above having a physical side.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p16#3/r28.anchor: وبالجملة لا يمكن إبقاء الكلام على حقيقته لتنزهه عز وجل من الجنب بالمعنى الحقيقي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r1.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r1.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah has fi dhikr Allah, in remembrance of God, in place of the phrase in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r1.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله زحفصة ( في ذكر الله )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r2.claim: The speaker says that he used to mock God's religion and its people.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r2.anchor: أي المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وأهله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r3.claim: In is the lightened form of heavy inna, and the lām is the differentiating particle.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r3.anchor: و ( إن ) المخففة من الثقيلة واللام هي الفارقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r4.claim: Zamakhshari takes the clause as circumstantial: the speaker neglected God's due while mocking.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r4.anchor: والجملة في محل النصب على الحال عند الزمخشري أي فرطت في حال سخريتي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r5.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r5.claim: Al-Bahr considers it an independent statement about the speaker's former worldly state, intended to inform and intensify regret, not a circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p17/r5.anchor: وقال في البحر : ويظهر أنها استئناف إخبار عن نفسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r1.claim: Here an means lest a soul say this; the construction parallels 16:15, where the mountains were set lest the earth sway with people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r1.anchor: يعني: لئلا تقول نفس، كقوله: "وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r2.speaker: المبرد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains the warning as an urging to act quickly and beware of reaching the point of saying this.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: أي بادروا واحذروا أن تقول نفس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads the phrase as expressing fear that people will reach a state in which they utter this regret.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: خوف أن تصيروا إلى حال تقولون هذا القول،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r4.claim: Hasrata means my regret; tahassur is grief over what has passed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r4.anchor: يا ندامتا، والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r5.claim: The intended form is my regret, but Arabic exclamations turn possessive yāʾ into alif, sometimes restoring yāʾ afterward to mark possession.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r5.anchor: وأراد: يا حسرتي، على الإضافة، لكن العرب تحول ياء الكناية ألفا في الاستغاثة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r6.claim: Abu Jaafar reads ya hasratai, restoring the possessive yāʾ after the alif.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r7.claim: Another explanation addresses regret itself: O regret, this is your moment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r7.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله: "يا حسرتا" يا أيتها الحسرة هذا وقتك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r8.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r8.anchor: قال الحسن: قصرت في طاعة الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r9.claim: Mujahid explains it as falling short in God's command.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r10.claim: Saeed ibn Jubayr explains it as neglecting God's right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r10.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: في حق الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r11.claim: Another view takes it to mean wasting one's effort in God's cause or essence.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r12.claim: A further view understands it as falling short on the path that leads to God's pleasure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه قصرت في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضاء الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r13.claim: The Arabs use janb to mean a side.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r14.claim: The regretful soul had mocked God's religion, Book, Messenger, and believers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r14.anchor: المستهزئين بدين الله وكتابه ورسوله والمؤمنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r15.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r15.claim: Qatada says the person not only neglected obedience but also mocked those who obeyed God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129/r15.anchor: قال قتادة: لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى جعل يسخر بأهل طاعته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r4.claim: The phrase means “lest a soul say”; نفس is indefinite because the speaker is one of some souls or to indicate abundance, as in al-Aʿshā’s verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r4.anchor: كراهة أن تقول وتنكير { نفس } لأن القائل بعض الأنفس

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r5.speaker: الأعشى
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r5.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line illustrates the rhetorical use of an indefinite noun for an individual or abundance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r5.anchor: كقول الأعشى: ورب بقيع لو هتفت بجوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r6.claim: A variant retains the original final yāʾ in “my regret.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r6.anchor: { يا حسرتى } وقرىء بالياء على الأصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r7.claim: The regret is for what the person neglected or fell short in doing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.claim: God’s “side” means His claim or right, namely obedience; alternatives take it as His essence with an omitted annexed word or His nearness as in 4:36; a reading says remembrance of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r8.anchor: في جانبه أي في حقه وهو طاعته

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.speaker: سابق البربري
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.claim: Sābiq al-Barbarī’s verse is evidence for جنب meaning a loved one’s right or claim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r9.anchor: قال سابق البربري: أما تتقين الله في جنب وامق

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.claim: The expression is a forceful allusion, like placing generosity and nobility within a dome built over a man.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r10.anchor: وهو كناية فيها مبالغة كقوله: إن السماحة والمروءة والندى

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.claim: The clause is accusative as a circumstantial statement: the speaker neglected God’s right while mocking.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:54-56/r11.anchor: ومحل { إن كنت } نصب على الحال كأنه قال فرطت وأنا ساخر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r6.claim: The construction means “lest a soul say” when torment arrives; the singular indefinite noun warns that anyone might be intended.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r6.anchor: ولما كان الموقع للإنسان في النقصان إنما هو حظوظه وشهواته المخالفة لعقله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r7.claim: Ḥasra is grief and regret for what has passed; the alif replacing yāʾ intensifies the cry of grief at discovering too late what would have benefited the soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r7.anchor: والتحسير : الاغتنام على ما فات والتندم عليه , وألحق الألف بدلا من الياء تعظيما له

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads ḥasratāya, retaining the original yāʾ alongside its replacement alif to intensify regret.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r8.anchor: ودل على تجاوز هذا التحسر الحد قراءة أبي جعفر ( حسرتاي ) بالجميع بين العوض وهو الألف والمعوض عنه وهو الياء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r9.claim: The cry laments that what was beneficial becomes clear only after it is too distant to recover.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r9.anchor: أي يا طول غماه لانكشاف ما فيه صلاحي عني وبعده مني فلا وصول لي إليه لاستدراك ما فات منه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r10.claim: The speaker admits wasting what was entrusted to them, so its order was broken and cannot be restored.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r10.anchor: أي بما ضيعت فانفرط مني نظامه , وتعذر انضمامه والتئامه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r11.claim: “God's side” refers to His right, close in sense as well as proximity; the side supports what is beside it, so neglecting it shows heedlessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r11.anchor: بالجنب قوام الشيء ولكنه قد يفرط فيه لكونه منحرفاعن الوجاه والعيان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r12.claim: Naming God rather than using a pronoun heightens the warning: the supreme King's right was neither forgotten nor treated lightly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r12.anchor: وصرف القول إلى الاسم الأعظم لزيادة التهويل بقوله : { الله } أي حق الملك الأعظم الذي هو غير مغفول عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r13.claim: The speaker admits mockery was habitual: sin was not enough, for they also mocked the obedient and arrogantly considered themselves right.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r13.anchor: أي المستهزئين المتكبرين المنزلين أنفسهم في غير منزلتها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r14.claim: In distress, people plead for pardon and hope to be restored to better circumstances, as this speaker now does.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r14.anchor: على عادة المترققين في وقت الشدائد , لعلهم يعادون إلى أجمل العوائد

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God foretells what people will say and do before they say or know it, linking this to 35:14.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت} الآيات قال أخبر الله سبحانه ما العباد قائلون قبل أن يقولوه

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss is textually damaged here, with a blank preceding المحلوقين.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r6.claim: Qatāda says one group neglected obedience and then mocked God's obedient servants.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين} قال: فلم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues returned people still could not attain guidance and would repeat former conduct, citing 6:28 and 6:110.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains neglect in God's regard as neglecting God's remembrance.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {على ما فرطت في جنب الله} قال: في ذكر الله

DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.claim: Qatāda says the three regrets belong to different classes of people.
DURR-FULL:v7p240/r11.anchor: قال: هذا قول صنف منهم {أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين} قال: هذا قول صنف منهم آخر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3254/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3254/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3254/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God disclosed what people would say and do before they said or did it. He explains the regret as lamenting neglect of God’s due and mockery, followed by excuses that they were not guided or should be returned; scripture says they would lie and return to their former conduct, and they would again be barred from guidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3254/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله : ان تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت . . الايات . قال : اخبر الله سبحانه ما العباد قائلون قبل ان يقولوه وعملهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r1.claim: ‘Lest a soul say’ gives the reason for the commands in verses 54–55, with the purpose lam omitted before an; this omission is common.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r2.claim: A negative la is omitted after an, a common construction illustrated by verses about following the Quran and not following desire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r2.anchor: وفيه حذف لا } النافية بعد { أن ، وهو شائع أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf commonly supplies the omitted sense as ‘for fear that you do such and such.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur finds an omitted negative la clearer than al-Kashshaf’s paraphrase, since Arabic uses deletion and addition of la frequently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r4.anchor: أظهر لكثرة التصرف فيها في كلام العرب بالحذف والزيادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r5.claim: The soul says this so it will not lament its neglect of God’s cause. The words may be an audible cry of regret, adding to hidden regret, or inward speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r5.anchor: وظاهر القول إنه القول جهرة وهو شأن الذي ضاق صبره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r6.claim: The indefinite ‘a soul’ names a category, namely polytheist souls, like the generic soul in the verse about what each soul knows it has brought.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r6.anchor: أن يقول صنف من النفوس وهي نفوس المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r7.claim: Labid’s line about death seizing ‘some souls’ uses the plural to mean himself, illustrating a generic or indefinite soul.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r8.claim: The vocative personifies intense regret as a rational being summoned to appear when needed; the formula became a common saying for extreme sorrow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r8.anchor: بتشبيه الحسرة بالعاقل الذي ينادي ليقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r9.claim: Hasra is intense remorse, and the alif in the expression substitutes for the speaker’s ya.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r10.claim: Abu Ja‘far alone reads ya hasratai, combining the speaker’s ya with the alif that normally replaces it; his most common reported form has the ya after alif open.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحده { يا حسرتاي } بالجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r11.claim: Using ‘upon’ with hasra, as is usual, depicts the regret as firmly pressing upon its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p44#2/r11.anchor: بحرف الاستعلاء كما هو غالبها للدلالة على تمكن التحسر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r1.claim: Ma in ‘for what I neglected’ is a verbal noun, so the phrase means ‘for my neglect.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r1.anchor: أي على تفريطي في جنب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r2.claim: Tafrit means wasting or falling short; the more usual expression is to say farraṭa fīhi.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r3.claim: Janb and janib both mean a thing’s side or vicinity; al-sahib bi-l-janb in 4:36 means a neighboring companion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r3.anchor: والجنب والجانب مترادفان ، وهو ناحية الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r4.claim: One analysis makes fi complete the verb without a direct object: God’s ‘side’ means His cause, right, attributes, and commands, metaphorically pictured as a master’s neglected preserve; Sabiq al-Barbari’s verse illustrates the wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون لتعدية فعل فرطت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r5.claim: Alternatively, the phrase depicts the judged soul as a servant who neglected a master’s sanctuary and livestock; this tableau lets janb retain its literal sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r5.anchor: لحال النفس التي أوقفت للحساب والعقاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r6.claim: Alternatively, ma is a relative pronoun, farraṭt has a deleted object pronoun referring to it, and the prepositional phrase describes that object: what I neglected in God’s side.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r6.anchor: ويكون المفعول محذوفا وهو الضمير المحذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r7.claim: The declarative phrase performs regret for failing to accept the Messenger’s guidance and mocking him; as a circumstantial clause, it admits neglect like a mocker rather than an unaware person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r7.anchor: خبر مستعمل في إنشاء الندامة على ما فاتها من قبول ما جاءها به الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r8.claim: In is the lightened form of emphatic inna, while the lām in ‘among the mockers’ distinguishes it from negative in.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r9.claim: ‘Among the mockers’ more emphatically attributes mockery than ‘a mocker’; Ibn Ashur notes a similar construction in the Quran’s wording about being among the ignorant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p46/r9.anchor: أشد مبالغة في الدلالة على اتصافهم بالسخرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.claim: The statements follow the natural movement of thought at judgment: regret, then excuse, then wish for a return to do good. Reordering them would lose the signal of how these thoughts arise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p47/r5.anchor: الأصل في الإنشاء ما لم يوجد ما يقتضي العدول عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.claim: The reply pairs the guidance excuse with signs that came and were denied, neglect with the greater offense of arrogance, and the wish to be God-fearing with being a disbeliever; Quranic guidance left no excuse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r3.anchor: أن الله هداك في الدنيا بالإرشاد بآيات القرآن فقابلت الإرشاد بالتكذيب والاستكبار والكفر بها فلا عذر لك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.claim: The answer uses a deliberately scrambled distribution after a summary: it first dispatches the main excuse, then neglect, then the return wish. It skips the mockery claim because that was already an admission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p48/r4.anchor: وكان الجواب على طريقة النشر المشوش بعد اللف رعيا لمقتضى ذلك التشويش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r1.claim: The opening an-clause gives the purpose: return and submit so that a soul will not say these things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r1.anchor: أن في هذه الآية مفعول من أجله أي أنيبوا وأسلموا من أجل أن تقول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r2.claim: Most readers have yā ḥasratī; Arabs also replace the possessive yāʾ with alif, as in yā ghulāmā and yā jārā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «يا حسرتي» والأصل «يا حسرتي» ، ومن العرب من يرد ياء الإضافة ألفا فيقول: يا غلاما ويا جارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads yā ḥasratāy with fatḥa on the yāʾ, also reported with the yāʾ quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع: «يا حسرتاي» بفتح الياء، ورويت عنه بسكون الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r4.speaker: أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ objects that this form combines a substitute with what it substitutes for.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: جمع بين العوض والمعوض منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r5.speaker: ابن جماز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jammāz reports from Abū Jaʿfar a reading with kasra on tāʾ and a quiescent yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r5.anchor: وروى ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر: «يا حسرتي» بكسر التاء وسكون الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r6.claim: Sībawayh explains the vocative of regret or woe as summoning it to arrive because this is its time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: ومعنى نداء الحسرة والويل، أي هذا وقتك وزمانك فاحضري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r7.claim: Farraṭtu means that the speaker fell short in what was required.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r7.anchor: و: فرطت معناه: قصرت في اللازم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r8.claim: Fī janb Allāh means in matters directed toward God and the sphere of His obedience: neglecting His law and faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: في جنب الله معناه: في مقاصدي إلى الله وفي جهة طاعته، أي في تضييع شريعته والإيمان به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r9.claim: Janb is used figuratively for such matters, as illustrated by the cited poetic expression about blame in Bakr's cause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r9.anchor: والجنب: يعبر به عن هذا ونحوه. ومنه قول الشاعر: [الطويل] أفي جنب بكر قطعتني ملامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains fī janb Allāh as meaning in God's affair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: في جنب الله أي في أمر الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r11.claim: The speaker regrets having mocked God's command; sukhriyya means mockery.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r11.anchor: وقول الكافر: وإن كنت لمن الساخرين ندامة على استهزائه بأمر الله تعالى. والسخر: الاستهزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.claim: The two later occurrences of aw taqūlu coordinate with the first an taqūla clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12.anchor: وقوله: أو تقول في الموضعين عطف على قوله: أن تقول الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r1.speaker: المبرد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad construes the phrase as urging people to act before a soul says this, or as cautioning them against its saying it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r1.anchor: قال المبرد المعنى بادروا قبل أن تقول نفس وحذرا من أن تقول نفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes it as fear that people will reach a state in which they say these words.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج خوف أن تصيروا إلى حال تقولون فيها هذا القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r3.claim: Ya hasrata means “my regret” or “my sorrow”; grief is distress over what has passed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r3.anchor: ومعنى ﴿ يا حسرتى ﴾ يا ندامتا ويا حزنا والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r4.claim: The alif in ya hasrata stands for the first-person yāʾ, so the phrase is possessive: “my regret.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r4.anchor: والألف في يا حسرتا هي ياء المتكلم والمعنى يا حسرتي على الإضافة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r5.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic changes the possessive yāʾ to alif in expressions of appeal, giving them the form of a supplication.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r5.anchor: قال الفراء والعرب تحول الياء إلى الألف في كل كلام معناه الاستغاثة ويخرج على لفظ الدعاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r6.claim: Arabic may add hāʾ after this alif, with the hāʾ read either with kasra or ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r6.anchor: وربما أدخلت العرب الهاء بعد هذه الألف فيخفضونها مرة ويرفعونها أخرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r7.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية وأبو عمران وأبو الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu al-Aliya, Abu Imran, and Abu al-Jawza read ya hasrati with kasra on the tāʾ, as a possessive construction referring to the soul.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو العالية وأبو عمران وأبو الجوزاء يا حسرتي بكسر التاء على الإضافة إلى النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r8.speaker: معاذ القارئ وأبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r8.claim: Muadh al-Qari and Abu Ja'far read ya hasrata with an alif after the tāʾ and an open yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r8.anchor: وقرأ معاذ القارئ وأبو جعفر يا حسرتاي بألف بعد التاء وياء مفتوحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r9.speaker: النحويون أجمعون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r9.claim: Al-Farra allows forms with a final hāʾ in several case vowels, but all grammarians reject retaining that hāʾ in connected speech.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج وزعم الفراء أنه يجوز يا حسرتاه على كذا بفتح الهاء ويا حسرتاه بالضم والكسر والنحويون أجمعون لا يجيزون أن تثبت هذه الهاء مع الوصل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan interprets “in God's side” as in God's obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r1.anchor: في طاعة الله تعالى قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets it as God's due or right.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r2.anchor: في حق الله قاله سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Zajjaj interpret it as God's command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r3.anchor: في أمر الله قاله مجاهد والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r4.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak interpret it as remembrance of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r4.anchor: في ذكر الله قاله عكرمة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra reads janb as nearness, using the Arabic idiom for living near someone; the regret is failing to seek nearness to God, namely Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r5.anchor: روي عن الفراء أنه قال الجنب القرب أي في قرب الله وجواره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r6.claim: The speaker admits having mocked the Quran and believers in worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p192#2/r6.anchor: أي وما كنت إلا من المستهزئين بالقرآن وبالمؤمنين في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r4.claim: The clause is a purpose complement to the preceding commands of repentance, sincerity, and following the Qur’an.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r4.anchor: مفعول له للأفعال السابقة التي هي الإنابة والإخلاص ، واتباع القرآن والتنكير ؛

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r5.claim: The indefinite soul can mean some souls, or can generalize the warning so it applies throughout all souls.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r5.anchor: والتنكير ؛ لأن القائل بعض الأنفس ، أو للتكثير والتعميم ليشيع في كل النفوس.

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r6.claim: The commands are given so that no person will later say the words of regret described here.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r6.anchor: والمعنى : افعلوا ما ذكر من المأمورات ، يعني : أمرتكم به كراهة أن تقول كل نفس.

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r7.claim: The alif replaces the possessive yāʾ of the original yā ḥasratī; Arabic also uses several forms with alif and compensating yāʾ, and the cry is an appeal for help.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r7.anchor: يا حسرتى} بالألف بدلا من ياء الإضافة إذ أصله :

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r8.claim: Ḥasra is grief and regret over what was missed, as if the ignorance that led to the deed has been stripped away.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r8.anchor: والحسرة : الغم على ما فاته والندم عليه ؛ كأنه انحسر الجهل عنه الذي حمله على ما ارتكبه.

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r9.claim: Some define ḥasra as sorrow so intense that the soul is left exhausted and cut off.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الحسرة أن تأسف النفس أسفا تبقى منه حسيرا ؛ أي : منقطعة.

BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r10.claim: The speaker calls regret to come near: now is the time for it to appear.
BURSEVI:v8p96#3/r10.anchor: والمعنى : يا حسرتي وندامتي احضري ، فهذا أوان حضورك.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r1.claim: The phrase means my negligence and shortcoming; mā is a verbal noun particle.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r1.anchor: {على ما فرطت} ؛ أي : على تفريطي وتقصيري ، فما مصدرية.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p97/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes excess in pressing ahead from tafrīṭ, which is falling short because farṭ means what precedes.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r2.anchor: قال الراغب : الإفراط أن يسرف في التقدم. والتفريط أن يقصر فإن الفرط المتقدم.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r3.claim: God’s side means His obedience, fulfilling His due, and following His path.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r3.anchor: {فى جناب الله} في جانبه ، وهو طاعته وإقامة حقه وسلوك طريقه.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r4.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p97/r4.claim: Kashf al-asrār notes that Arabs use janb for a side or flank.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r4.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" العرب تسمي الجانب جنبا.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p97/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says janb originally means a bodily limb, then denotes the adjacent side, as with right and left.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب : أصل الجنب الجارحة جمعه جنوب ، ثم استعير في الناحية التي تليها كاستعارة سائر الجوارح

BURSEVI:v8p97/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r6.claim: In God's side means neglecting His command alone, in the form He prescribed for people.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r6.anchor: وقوله : في جنب الله ؛ أي : في أمره وحده الذي حده لنا. انتهى.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r7.claim: In is lightened, the lām distinguishes it, and the clause is accusative as a circumstantial phrase; sakhr means mockery.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r7.anchor: إن هي المخففة واللام هي الفارقة. والسخر : الاستهزاء ، ومحل الجملة النصب على الحال.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r8.claim: The speaker admits neglect while in worldly life mocking God's religion and its adherents.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r8.anchor: والمعنى فرطت ، والحال : أني كنت في الدنيا من المستهزئين بدين الله وأهله.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r9.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v8p97/r9.claim: Qatāda says they not only neglected obedience to God but also mocked those who obeyed Him.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r9.anchor: قال قتادة : لم يكفهم ما ضيعوا من طاعة الله حتى سخروا بأهل طاعته.

BURSEVI:v8p97/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p97/r10.claim: A Persian poem depicts death awakening the heedless to years of sin, displaying each deed, and bringing regret that can no longer help.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r10.anchor: در سلسلة الذهب فرمود : روز آخر كه مرك مردم خوار كند از خواب غفلتش بيدار يادش آيدكه

BURSEVI:v8p97/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p97/r11.speaker: الفارسي
BURSEVI:v8p97/r11.claim: Al-Fārisī says the one who flees from God to the self is burned by regret at missing Him when seeing the knowers' stations; only such anguish produces this cry.
BURSEVI:v8p97/r11.anchor: قال الفارسي : يقول الله تعالى : من هرب مني أحرقته ؛ أي : من هرب مني إلى نفسه أحرقته بالتأسف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r2.claim: On Judgment Day the criminal who neglected repentance and return to God will regret it and wish he had been among the sincere, obedient doers of good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r2.anchor: أي: يوم القيامة يتحسر المجرم المفرط في التوبة والإنابة، ويود لو كان من المحسنين المخلصين المطيعين لله عز وجل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r3.claim: The regretful person admits that his worldly conduct was that of a scoffer who mocked rather than a believer with certainty and conviction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r3.anchor: أي: إنما كان عملي في الدنيا عمل ساخر مستهزئ غير موقن مصدق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God disclosed what people would say before they said it and what they would do before acting; Ibn Kathir cites 35:14 in support.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r5.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة: عن ابن عباس: أخبر الله سبحانه (4) ، ما العباد قائلون قبل أن يقولوه،

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yā ḥasratāy with a yāʾ after alif, as in bushrāy.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر: يا حسرتاي بياء بعد الألف مثل: (بشراي).

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r2.claim: The other readers omit the yāʾ after alif, as in bushrā and yā asafā.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يا حسرتا بغير ياء مثل: بشرى، ويا [أسفا]

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r3.claim: The alif represents the speaker's possessive yāʾ; Arabs replace that yāʾ with alif in cries to lengthen the sound.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r3.anchor: والألف فيه تدل على ياء الإضافة، وهو كناية عن المتكلم، وتقديره: يا حسرتاي على الإضافة

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line with hāʾ attached; some readers append yāʾ after alif to make the possessive explicit.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r4.anchor: أنشد الفراء: يا مرحباه بحمار ناجيه وربما يلحقون به الياء بعد الألف لتحقيق الإضافة على قراءة أبي جعفر

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r12.claim: Nafs and dhawāt refer to the same thing; nafs derives from preciousness, since the self is an animal's most precious part.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r12.anchor: النفس والذوات واحد، وأصله من النفاسة، فأنفس ما يكون في الحيوان نفسه، وهو عينه.

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r13.claim: Taḥassur, regret, and sorrow are near-synonyms for grief over what has passed; ḥasra is intense regret.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r13.anchor: والتحسر والتندم والتأسف من النظائر وهو: الاغتمام بما فات وقته، وأصل الحسرة: شدة الندم

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r14.claim: “O my regret” means regret for themselves; regret cannot literally be summoned, so the cry alerts listeners.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r14.anchor: ويا حسرتا أي: يا حسرتهم على أنفسهم، قال الأزهري: قد علم أن الحسرة لا تدعى، ودعاؤها تنبيه للمخاطبين

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r15.speaker: الأزهري
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r15.claim: Al-Azharī explains the cry as if the speaker says, “My regret, answer; now is your time.”
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r15.anchor: كأنه يقول: يا حسرتاي أجيبي فهذا وقتك

JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r16.claim: The root conveys exhaustion: a camel is ḥasirat when its journey ends from fatigue, like the regretful person.
JISHUMI:v8p6082#2/r16.anchor: وأصل الباب: هو الانقطاع، يقال: حسرت الناقة أي: انقطع سيرها كلالا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r16.claim: The clause can mean “lest a soul say” or “that a soul not say.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r16.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : معناه لئلا تقول نفس . الثاني : أن لا تقول نفس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r17.claim: The alif in حسرتا replaces possessive yā' and lengthens an exclamation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r17.anchor: والألف التي في يا حسرتا بدل من ياء الإضافة ففعل ذلك في الاستغاثة لمدة الصوت بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r18.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r18.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say it means neglecting God's command.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r18.anchor: في مجانبة أمر الله ، قاله مجاهد والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r19.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r19.claim: Al-Hasan says it refers to God's essence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r20.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r20.claim: Al-Suddi says it means neglecting remembrance of God, here the Qur'an.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r20.anchor: في ذكر الله ، قاله السدي ، وذكر الله هنا القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r21.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r21.claim: Al-Naqqash says it means forfeiting God's reward in Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r21.anchor: في ثواب الله من الجنة حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r22.claim: One view equates جنب and جانب, the side leading to God's pleasure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r22.anchor: في الجانب المؤدي إلى رضا الله ، والجنب والجانب سواء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r23.claim: Another view means seeking closeness to God, as الصاحب بالجنب means someone nearby.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r23.anchor: في طلب القرب من الله ومنه قوله تعالى { والصاحب بالجنب } أي بالقرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r24.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r24.claim: Al-Naqqash says the speaker mocked the Qur'an in worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r24.anchor: أحدهما : من المستهزئين في الدنيا بالقرآن , قاله النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r25.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r25.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says the speaker mocked the Prophet and believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p131/r25.anchor: الثاني : بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالمؤمنين , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MUJAHID:v2p559#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p559#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p559#3/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the regret as neglecting what God commanded.
MUJAHID:v2p559#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله ﴾ يعني على ما ضيعت من أمر الله

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r2.anchor: أن تقول نفس يحسرتا } يعنى يا ندامتا

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r3.claim: To have fallen short means to have neglected something.
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r3.anchor: على ما فرطت } يعنى ما ضيعت { في جنب الله

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r4.claim: “In God’s side” means with respect to God, specifically in remembrance of Him.
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r4.anchor: في جنب الله } يعنى فى ذات الله يعنى من ذكر الله

MUQATIL:39:55-60/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r5.claim: The regretful person mocked the Qur’an in this world.
MUQATIL:39:55-60/r5.anchor: يعنى لمن المستهزئين بالقرآن فى الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.claim: An taqūla means lest a soul say.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ أن تقول ﴾ لئلا تقول ﴿ نفس ﴾ إنما نكرت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.claim: The indefinite soul may mean some souls, specifically unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.anchor: إنما نكرت لأن المرد بها بعض الأنفس وهى نفس الكافر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it can be a distinctive individual soul, exceptionally stubborn in disbelief or facing terrible punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد نفس متميزة من الأنفس اما بلجاج فى الكفر شديد أو بعذاب عظيم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.claim: The indefinite may also be used generically for a multitude.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.claim: The alif in yā ḥasratā substitutes for the speaker's yāʾ; readings preserve the original yāʾ or combine the substitute and what it replaces.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.anchor: الألف بدل من ياء المتكلم وقرىء يا حسرتى على الأصل ويا حسرتاى على الجمع بين العوض والمعوض منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.claim: Farraṭtu means I fell short; mā is a verbal noun, as in the expression bi-mā raḥubat.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.anchor: قصرت وما مصدرية مثلها فى بما رحبت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.claim: Fī janbi Allāh can mean in God's affair, in His obedience, or with regard to His essence; ʿAbd Allāh's reading has fī dhikr Allāh.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.anchor: فى أمر الله أو فى طاعة الله أو فى ذاته وفى حرف عبد الله فى ذكر الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.claim: Janb literally means side or vicinity; saying someone fell short at God's side means he neglected God's due, a metonymy based on locating an act in someone's sphere.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.anchor: والجنب الجانب يقال أنا فى جنب فلان وجانبه وناحيته وفلان لين الجانب والجنب ثم قالوا فرط فى جنبه وفى جانبه يريدون فى حقه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.claim: A report calls a man praying for another man's sake a form of hidden shirk, illustrating the expression li-makān al-rajul, for the man's sake.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.anchor: ومنه الحديث من الشرك الخفى أن يصلى الرجل لمكان الرجل أى لأجله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains it as falling short in God's path: affirming His oneness and Muhammad's prophethood.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه فرط فى طريق الله وهو توحيده والاقرار بنبوة محمد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r11.claim: Qatāda says the unbeliever not only neglected God's obedience but mocked those who obeyed Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r11.anchor: قال قتادة لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى سخر من أهلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r12.claim: The inna clause is accusative as a circumstantial phrase: I neglected God's due while mocking.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p60#2/r12.anchor: ومحل وإن كنت النصب على الحال كأنه قال فرطت وأنا ساخر أى فرطت فى حال سخريتى

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r14.claim: The phrase an taqūla is accusative: al-Kisāʾī’s school takes it as “lest a soul say,” al-Baṣrans as “for fear that it say,” and another view supplies “before a soul says” from the preceding clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r14.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أن تقول نفس يحسرتا } { أن } في موضع نصب أي كراهة { أن تقول } وعند الكوفيين لئلا تقول

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the indefinite “a soul” as a particular unbelieving soul, perhaps marked by obstinate disbelief or severe punishment; it may also be generic and refer to many souls.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r15.anchor: الزمخشري: فإن قلت لم نكرت؟ قلت: لأن المراد بها بعض الأنفس وهي نفس الكافر.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r16.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses an indefinite cemetery to mean groups of generous men, supporting the reading of nafs as a generic plurality rather than one person.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:54-56/r16.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد التكثير كما قال الأعشى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r1.claim: Ḥasrata is an expression of regret; the original yā ḥasratī changed its final yāʾ to alif because alif is lighter and lets the cry be prolonged.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r1.anchor: «يا حسرتا» والأصل «يا حسرتي» فأبدل من الياء ألف لأنها أخف وأمكن في الاستغاثة بمد الصوت

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line with hāʾ appended to the cry, while al-Qurṭubī notes that a yāʾ may also be appended after the alif to mark possession.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r2.anchor: وربما ألحقوا بها الهاء أنشد الفراء: يا مرحباه بحمار ناجيه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the cry as yā ḥasratāy, with a yāʾ after the alif to show possession.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r3.anchor: وكذلك قرأها أبو جعفر: «يا حسرتاي» والحسرة الندامة.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets “in God’s side” as in God’s obedience.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets it as neglecting God’s remembrance, meaning the Qur’an and acting by it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أي في ذكر الله عز وجل. قال: يعني القرآن والعمل به.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains “in God’s side” as in God’s reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: «في جنب الله» أي في ثواب الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r8.speaker: الفراء
