QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says janb means nearness or neighborliness; the phrase means failing to seek God’s nearness and Paradise, as in the Qur’anic “companion by the side.”
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء: الجنب القرب والجوار يقال فلان يعيش في جنب فلان أي في جواره

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r9.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it means neglecting the path God called people to; Arabs call a means or road to something its janb, as in doing something for another’s sake and pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r9.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي على ما فرطت في الطريق الذي هو طريق الله الذي دعاني إليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r10.claim: Another explanation is the side leading to God’s pleasure and reward; a poet’s line uses janb for a side or party.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r10.anchor: وقيل: «في جنب الله» أي في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضا الله عز وجل وثوابه،

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r11.speaker: ابن عرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r11.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says it means neglecting God’s affair, supported by the idiom “I did not do that in the side of my need” and a line by Kathīr.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عرفة: أي تركت من أمر الله يقال ما فعلت ذلك في جنب حاجتي

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r12.claim: Mujāhid likewise interprets the phrase as having neglected God’s affair.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r12.anchor: وكذا قال مجاهد أي ضيعت من أمر الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r13.claim: A report from the Prophet says a person who sits, walks or lies down without remembering God incurs a “tirah,” meaning regret on the Day of Resurrection; Abū Dāwūd relates it in this sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r13.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r14.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r14.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Taymī lists three regrets at the Resurrection: another inheriting and rightly using one’s wealth, a former slave being nearer God, and a worldly blind acquaintance seeing while one is blind.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r14.anchor: وقال إبراهيم التيمي: من الحسرات يوم القيامة أن يرى الرجل ماله الذي أتاه الله في الدنيا يوم القيامة في ميزان غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r15.claim: The speaker says that in worldly life he mocked the Qur’an, the Messenger and God’s allies.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r15.anchor: أي وما كنت إلا من المستهزئين بالقرآن وبالرسول في الدنيا وبأولياء الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r16.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r16.claim: Qatāda says the sinner not only neglected obedience to God but also mocked those who obeyed Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى سخر من أهلها.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r17.claim: Inna kuntu is accusative as a circumstantial clause: the speaker neglected duty while mocking.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r17.anchor: ومحل «إن كنت» النصب على الحال كأنه قال: فرطت وأنا ساخر

QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r18.claim: Another explanation is that the speaker lived only in mockery, play and falsehood, or that his activity amounted to worshipping other than God.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r18.anchor: وقيل وما كنت إلا في سخرية ولعب وباطل أي ما كان سعيي إلا في عبادة غير الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r7.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ tells of a learned Israelite who read that final deeds determine one’s end, abandoned worship for sin after Satan promised time to repent, squandered his wealth, then died in pleasure and regretted spending his life obeying Satan; the account says God revealed his story in the Qur’an.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r7.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: كان رجل عالم في بني إسرائيل وجد رقعة: إن العبد ليعمل الزمان الطويل بطاعة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.claim: Qatāda distinguishes three groups: one regrets neglecting God’s affair, another says God should have guided it, and the third wishes for another return to become righteous.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: هؤلاء أصناف صنف منهم قال: { يحسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله }.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r16.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r16.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects the objection: the implied sense is “among the group of mockers,” “people,” or “folk,” so the masculine plural need not change.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r16.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا لا يلزم ألا ترى أن قبله { أن تقول نفس } ثم قال: { وإن كنت لمن الساخرين }

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r5.claim: “That a soul should say” is in the accusative as a purpose expression, meaning lest or for fear that it should say this.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r5.anchor: مفعول له أي كراهة أن تقول

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r6.claim: The indefinite “a soul” may denote a particular soul distinguished by especially persistent sin.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r6.anchor: يجوز أن تراد نفس ممتازة عن سائر النفوس لأجل اختصاصها بمزيد إضرار بما لا ينفي رغبتها في المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r7.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite noun can be general: because regret naturally follows neglect of obedience, the construction implies that such regret occurs for every such neglect.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6/r7.anchor: علم أصول الفقه أن الحكم المذكور عقيب وصف يناسبه

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.claim: Those who affirm divine bodily parts cite “God’s side,” but Razi rejects bodily meaning because arguments against divine parts require interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.anchor: واعلم أن دلائلنا على نفي الأعضاء قد كثرت

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains neglecting God’s side as forfeiting God’s reward.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد ضيعت من ثواب الله

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r3.claim: Mقاتل explains it as neglecting remembrance of God.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل ضيعت من ذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r4.claim: Mujahid explains it as neglecting God’s command.

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan explains it as neglecting obedience to God.

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains it as neglecting God’s due.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير في حق الله

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r7.claim: Razi derives “side” from a thing’s aspect or component and extends it by analogy to what belongs to or follows from a thing, such as God’s cause, command, or obedience; a poetic line supports the usage.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r7.anchor: الجنب سمي جنبا لأنه جانب من جوانب ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports “ya hasratī” as the original form and “ya hasratāy” as combining the substitute with what it replaces.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) قرىء { * يا حسرتي } على الأصل

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r9.claim: The sinner says he not only neglected obedience but also mocked religion and its adherents.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r9.anchor: أي أنه ما كان مكتفيا بذلك التقصير بل كان من المستهزئين بالدين

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r10.claim: Qatada says the sinner was not content with neglecting obedience but mocked those who practiced it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r10.anchor: قال قتادة لم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى سخر من أهلها

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r11.claim: The clause “though I was among the mockers” is accusative as a circumstantial clause: he neglected God’s cause while mocking.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r11.anchor: نصب على الحالة كأنه قال : فرطت في جنب الله وأنا ساخر

RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r12.claim: The damned person voices three responses: regret at neglected obedience, an excuse that God did not guide him, and a wish to return and act well.
RAZI-FULL:v27p6#2/r12.anchor: أتى بثلاثة أشياء أولها : الحسرة على التفريط في الطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r2.claim: Al-Qadi adds that regret for neglected obedience, reproach for mockery, and the sinner’s claim that guidance would have enabled piety all presuppose that these acts were within human power.
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r2.anchor: ولا يتحسر المرء على أمر سبق منه إلا وكان يصح منه أن يفعله

RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r3.claim: Al-Qadi says the wishes for guidance, piety, another return, and good deeds make no sense if God gave the person only an unchangeable capacity for unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v27p7#2/r3.anchor: قال القاضي هذه الآيات دالة على صحة القول بالقدر

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r1.claim: The warning means that a person should not wait until it is too late before seeking repentance.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r1.anchor: Lest any soul should say, that is, lest anyone should seek to repent only when it is too late

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r2.claim: Alas for me expresses the utmost regret and grief for failing to perform God's enjoined deeds.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r2.anchor: Alas for me is understood as an expression of utmost regret and grief (R) for having failed to perform the deeds enjoined by God

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r3.claim: The phrase rendered “of my duty to God” literally means “of” or “from the side of God” and can mean God's Right.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r3.anchor: which literally means “of” or “from the side of God” and is interpreted to mean, “of God’s Right”

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r4.claim: Other interpretations of the phrase are neglecting obedience to God or missing God's reward.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r4.anchor: “of obedience to God” (Q, Ṭs, Z), or “of the reward of God”

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r5.claim: Arabic janb, “side,” can suggest bodily, emotional, or spiritual closeness; the phrase may mean nearness to God or Paradise, nearness to what leads to Him, or seeking His nearness.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r5.anchor: can allude to physical, emotional, and spiritual closeness, as when one speaks of being by another’s side in English.

STUDYQURAN:39:56/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r6.claim: The scoffers are those who mocked the Quran and the Messenger.
STUDYQURAN:39:56/r6.anchor: The scoffers are those who scoffed at the Quran and the Messenger

TAB-FULL:v20p233/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p233/r1.claim: “Lest a soul say” is the purpose of the commands to return and submit, with an implicit negation as in 16:15; hence the clause is in the accusative.
TAB-FULL:v20p233/r1.anchor: {أن تقول نفس} [الزمر: 56] بمعنى لئلا تقول نفس

TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {يا حسرتا} قال: «الندامة»

TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r2.claim: The ending alif stands for first-person yāʾ in “my sorrow”; Arabic turns that yāʾ into alif in cries of lament, such as “يا ويلتا” and “يا ندما.”
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r2.anchor: والألف في قوله {يا حسرتا} هي كناية المتكلم، وإنما أريد: يا حسرتي؛ ولكن العرب تحول الياء في كناية اسم المتكلم في الاستغاثة ألفا

TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r3.claim: Arabic also uses forms such as “يا حسرة على العباد” and “يا لهف/يا لهفا عليه”; al-Farraʾ cites Abū Thawrān's lowered “ألهف” as vocative genitive for self-directed lament.
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r3.anchor: وذكر الفراء أن أبا ثروان أنشده: [البحر الطويل]

TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports that Arabic may add hāʾ after the lament alif and inflect it with either genitive or nominative; a Banū Asad line illustrates this usage.
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r4.anchor: بعد هذه الألف، فيخفضونها أحيانا، ويرفعونها أحيانا؛ وذكر الفراء أن بعض بني أسد أنشد: [البحر الرجز] يا رب يا رباه إياك أسل

TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says lowering is the more common case, except in “يا هناه” and “يا هنتاه,” where nominative is more common because frequent use makes each expression seem like one word.
TAB-FULL:v20p233#2/r5.anchor: خفضا، قال: والخفض أكثر في كلامهم، إلا في قولهم: يا هناه، ويا هنتاه، فإن الرفع فيها أكثر من الخفض، لأنه كثير في الكلام، حتى صار كأنه حرف واحد

TAB-FULL:v20p235/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r1.claim: Neglecting one's duty “in God's regard” means failing to act on God's commands and falling short in obedience during worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله} يقول: «في أمر الله»

TAB-FULL:v20p235/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses “in God's regard” as “in God's command.”
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله} يقول: «في أمر الله»

TAB-FULL:v20p235/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase means abandoning what God commanded.
TAB-FULL:v20p235/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {على ما فرطت في جنب الله} [الزمر: 56] قال: «تركت من أمر الله»

TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r1.claim: The speaker regrets having mocked God's command, scripture, Messenger, and believers.
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين}

TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r2.claim: Qatada says this class not only neglected obedience but also mocked people who obeyed God.
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين} قال: " فلم يكفه أن ضيع طاعة الله حتى جعل يسخر بأهل طاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the mockery was directed at the Prophet, the Book, and the message he brought.
TAB-FULL:v20p235#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {وإن كنت لمن الساخرين} [الزمر: 56] يقول: «من المستهزئين بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالكتاب، وبما جاء به»

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.claim: The commands to repent and submit aim to prevent three afterlife regrets: sorrow for neglect, a claim that God did not guide, and a wish to return and act righteously.
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1.anchor: الله، وأن لا تقول نفس لأخرى: لو أن الله هداني للحق، فوفقني للرشاد

TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.claim: Qatada assigns the first regret to one class of people, the plea “if God had guided me” to a second, and the wish to return to a third.
TAB-FULL:v20p236/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله} الآية، قال: «هذا قول صنف منهم» {أو تقول لو أن الله هداني}

SULAMI:v2p202/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p202/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p202/r1.claim: Neglecting vigilance over God's due and constant service leads one to worldly immediacy, desire, and ego, wasting the aim of turning to and relying on God.
SULAMI:v2p202/r1.anchor: قال سهل : من ترك المراعات لحق الله وملازمة خدمته اشتغل بعاجل الدنيا ولذة الهوى

SULAMI:v2p202/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p202/r2.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p202/r2.claim: Faris says that whoever flees from God toward the self will be consumed by regret at missing Him when the stations of the knowers are seen tomorrow; only the spiritually consumed utter this lament.
SULAMI:v2p202/r2.anchor: قال فارس : يقول الله من هرب مني احرقته أي هرب مني إلى نفسه احرقته بالتأسف على فوتي

TUSTARI:39:56/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:39:56/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:39:56/r1.claim: The regret is for being occupied with immediate worldly life, appetite, and the ego, and neglecting pursuit of God, reliance on Him, His rights, and constant service.
TUSTARI:39:56/r1.anchor: اشتغلت بعاجل الدنيا ولذة الهوى ومتابعة النفس، وضيعت في جنب الله

TABATABAI:39:53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.claim: The passage calls people to Islam and following revelation, warns of regret for excess and worldly arrogance, and contrasts the pious’ salvation with unbelievers’ loss; its tone conveys mercy.
TABATABAI:39:53/r1.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يدعوهم إلى الإسلام واتباع ما أنزل الله ويحذرهم عما يستعقبه إسرافهم

TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.claim: These seven verses form one connected discourse: the ban on despair prepares for the following calls to repentance, submission, and righteous action, so the first verse is not an isolated promise.
TABATABAI:39:53-54/r4.anchor: كلام واحد ذو سياق واحد متصل ينهى عن القنوط

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r1.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r1.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines tafrīṭ as neglecting what must be done in time until its proper time passes.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r1.anchor: قال في المجمع التفريط إهمال ما يجب أن يتقدم فيه حتى يفوت وقته

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains regret as grief over something whose time has passed and which can no longer be recovered.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r2.anchor: وقال التحسر الاغتمام مما فات وقته لانحساره عنه بما لا يمكن استدراكه

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib says janb literally means a bodily side or limb, then is borrowed for the adjacent direction, like right and left.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r3.anchor: ثم يستعار في الناحية التي تليها لعادتهم في استعارة سائر الجوارح لذلك

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r4.claim: God’s side means what pertains to God and how the servant must treat it, concretely worshipping Him alone and not disobeying Him; neglect is falling short in that duty.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r4.anchor: فجنب الله جانبه وناحيته وهي ما يرجع إليه تعالى مما يجب على العبد أن يعامله ومصداق ذلك أن يعبده وحده ولا يعصيه

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r5.claim: In is softened from the heavy form, and al-sākhirīn is an active participle from sakhira, meaning to mock.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r5.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة، والساخرين اسم فاعل من سخر بمعنى استهزأ

TABATABAI:39:56-59/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r6.claim: The warning is meant to prevent a soul from lamenting its failure toward God and confessing that it mocked the truth; this speech occurs on Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:39:56-59/r6.anchor: إنما نخاطبكم بهذا الخطاب حذر أن تقول أو لئلا تقول نفس منكم يا حسرتا على ما قصرت في جانب الله

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r1.claim: The first utterance comes when the criminals see Judgment Day as the day of recompense and regret missed deeds, matching the lament in 6:31.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r1.anchor: حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.claim: The three sayings follow the order in which criminals would utter them; moving the reply to connect directly with its target would disrupt the arrangement.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r4.anchor: ثم لما نقل الأقوال على ما بينها من الترتيب أخذ في الجواب ولو أخر القول المجاب عنه حتى يتصل بالجواب

TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.claim: God does not answer the first and third sayings, about mocking truth and wishing to return, because He rebuffs the criminals and forbids them to speak, as 23:106–111 shows.
TABATABAI:39:57-61/r6.anchor: لأن في الأول حديث استهزائهم بالحق وأهله وفي الثالث تمنيهم للرجوع إلى الدنيا والله سبحانه يزجر هؤلاء يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.claim: Many reports from the Imams apply these verses to their Shiʿa and identify the side of God with them; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī classifies these as instances of application, not exegesis.
TABATABAI:39:53-61/r8.anchor: هناك روايات كثيرة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في تطبيق هذه الآيات على شيعتهم وتطبيق جنب الله عليهم وهي جميعا من الجري دون التفسير

TABRISI:39:56/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر والباقون
TABRISI:39:56/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yā ḥasratāya with yāʾ after alif; other readers omit it.
TABRISI:39:56/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر يا حسرتاي بياء مفتوحة بعد الألف والباقون يا حسرتا بغير ياء

TABRISI:39:56/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r2.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:39:56/r2.claim: Ibn Jinnī questions the reading because alif replaces yāʾ in ḥasratī, then explains it as combining substitute and replaced forms.
TABRISI:39:56/r2.anchor: قال ابن جني في قوله يا حسرتاي إشكال وذلك أن الألف في حسرتا إنما هي بدل من يا حسرتي

TABRISI:39:56/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
TABRISI:39:56/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s fumuwayhimā combines the mīm substitute with the wāw it replaces, a poetic parallel.
TABRISI:39:56/r3.anchor: قول الفرزدق: هما نفثا في في من فمويهما على النابح العاوي أشد رجام

TABRISI:39:56/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:39:56/r4.claim: Abū Zayd’s ‘yā Allāhumma, yā Allāhumā’ likewise combines the mīm substitute and replaced yāʾ.
TABRISI:39:56/r4.anchor: ما أنشده أبو زيد: إني إذا ما حدث ألما أقول يا اللهم يا اللهما

TABRISI:39:56/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56/r5.claim: Tafrīṭ neglects what must be done before time passes, like falling short and opposite prudent care.
TABRISI:39:56/r5.anchor: التفريط إهمال ما يجب أن يتقدم فيه حتى يفوت وقته ومثله التقصير وضده الأخذ بالحزم

TABRISI:39:56/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56/r6.claim: Taḥassur is grief for irretrievable loss; its root idea is becoming cut off.
TABRISI:39:56/r6.anchor: والتحسر الاغتمام مما فات وقته لانحساره عنه بما لا يمكنه لاستدراكه ومثله التأسف وأصل الباب الانقطاع

TABRISI:39:56/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56/r7.claim: Janb means bodily side and main or greatest part; idiom uses it for the matter of a need.
TABRISI:39:56/r7.anchor: والجنب العضو المعروف والجنب أيضا معظم الشيء وأكثره يقال هذا قليل في جنب مودتك

TABRISI:39:56/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r8.speaker: كثير
TABRISI:39:56/r8.claim: Kathīr’s line uses janb in the idiom ‘in the affair of a lover.’
TABRISI:39:56/r8.anchor: قال كثير: ألا تتقين الله في جنب عاشق له كبد حرى عليك تقطع

TABRISI:39:56/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56/r12.claim: Commands to obey and avoid reprehensible acts aim to prevent this regret; the clause means ‘for fear that’ or ‘lest.’
TABRISI:39:56/r12.anchor: لما أمر الله سبحانه باتباع الطاعات واجتناب المقبحات تحذيرا من نزول العقويات بين الغرض في ذلك بقوله { أن تقول نفس } أي خوف أن تقول

TABRISI:39:56/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:39:56/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as regret for wasting God’s reward.
TABRISI:39:56/r13.anchor: من ثواب الله عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:39:56/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r14.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:39:56/r14.claim: Mujāhid and al-Suddī say the speaker fell short in God’s command.
TABRISI:39:56/r14.anchor: قصرت في أمر الله عن مجاهد والسدي

TABRISI:39:56/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56/r15.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:39:56/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the speaker fell short in obedience to God.

TABRISI:39:56-60/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56-60/r1.claim: On al-Farrāʾ’s view, janb means nearness, so the regret is for failing to seek God’s proximity, that is, Paradise.
TABRISI:39:56-60/r1.anchor: فيكون المعنى على هذا القول على ما فرطت في طلب جنب الله أي في طلب جواره وقربه وهو الجنة

TABRISI:39:56-60/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:39:56-60/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says janb means side: the person fell short on God’s path toward His approval.
TABRISI:39:56-60/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي فرطت في الطريق الذي هو طريق الله فيكون الجنب بمعنى الجانب

TABRISI:39:56-60/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:39:56-60/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says, in a report through al-ʿAyyāshī and Abū al-Jārūd, ‘We are the side of God.’
TABRISI:39:56-60/r3.anchor: وروى العياشي بالإسناد عن أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر ع أنه قال: نحن جنب الله

TABRISI:39:56-60/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r4.speaker: قتادة والسدي
TABRISI:39:56-60/r4.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī say the speaker mocked the Prophet, Qurʾān, and believers in worldly life.
TABRISI:39:56-60/r4.anchor: المستهزئين بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن وبالمؤمنين في دار الدنيا عن قتادة والسدي

TABRISI:39:56-60/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:56-60/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:56-60/r5.claim: Another view says the speaker mocked those who called him to faith.
TABRISI:39:56-60/r5.anchor: وقيل: من الساخرين ممن يدعوني إلى الإيمان

FARRA:v2p421/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p421/r3.claim: The warning implies: act and repent so no soul says tomorrow, Alas for what I neglected; the same purpose construction in 16:15 means lest the earth sway you.
FARRA:v2p421/r3.anchor: وقوله: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى [56] أي افعلوا وأنيبوا وافعلوا (أن تقول نفس) ألا يقول أحدكم غدا (يا حسرتى)

FARRA:v2p421/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p421/r4.claim: يا حسرتى means alas for me; in appeals, Arabs turn the speaker’s final ya into alif, giving the utterance the form of a plea.
FARRA:v2p421/r4.anchor: وقوله: (يا حسرتى) : يا ويلتا مضاف إلى المتكلم يحول العرب الياء إلى الألف في كل كلام كان معناه الاستغاثة

FARRA:v2p421/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r5.speaker: أبو ثروان العكلي
FARRA:v2p421/r5.claim: His verse ألهفِ لأولاد uses genitive case, as in a vocative annexed by the speaker to himself.
FARRA:v2p421/r5.anchor: قال: أنشدني أبو ثروان العكلى. تزورونها أو لا أزور نساءكم ... ألهف لأولاد الإماء الحواطب

FARRA:v2p421/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p421/r6.speaker: أبو فقعس
FARRA:v2p421/r6.claim: Abu Fuq‘as’s يا رباه and يا مرحباه examples show added hā after alif; lowered case is more common, except يا هناه and يا هنتاه, where raising predominates.
FARRA:v2p421/r6.anchor: أنشدني أبو فقعس، بعض بني أسد: يا رب يا رباه إياك أسل ... عفراء يا رباه من قبل الأجل فخفض

THALABI:v8p245/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p245/r7.claim: The construction means lest a soul say, as in the constructions an tamīda bikum and an taṣūmū.
THALABI:v8p245/r7.anchor: أن تقول نفس يعني لأن لا تقول كقوله: أن تميد بكم وأن تصوموا

THALABI:v8p245/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p245/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p245/r8.claim: Yā ḥasratā means my regret and sorrow: grief over what is lost and cannot be recovered; Arabs replace the first-person yāʾ with alif in cries, sometimes adding hāʾ.
THALABI:v8p245/r8.anchor: يا حسرتى يا ندامتا وحزني، والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات

THALABI:v8p246/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v8p246/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the cry as yā ḥasratāy, retaining the possessive yāʾ after the alif.
THALABI:v8p246/r1.anchor: وكذلك قرأ أبو جعفر: يا حسرتاي.

THALABI:v8p246/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v8p246/r2.claim: Al-Farra cites the cry yā marḥabāh as evidence for the vocative alif form; Arabs may append yāʾ after the alif to mark possession.
THALABI:v8p246/r2.anchor: أنشد الفراء: يا مرحباه بحمار ناجية

THALABI:v8p246/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v8p246/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains falling short in God's side as falling short in obedience to God.

THALABI:v8p246/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v8p246/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains the phrase as falling short regarding God's right and affair.
THALABI:v8p246/r4.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: في حق الله في أمر الله.

THALABI:v8p246/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v8p246/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as falling short in God's affair.
THALABI:v8p246/r5.anchor: في حق الله في أمر الله. قاله مجاهد.

THALABI:v8p246/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v8p246/r6.claim: The language scholars explain the idiom as meaning in the matter of God, like calling something small beside a past affair.
THALABI:v8p246/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: هذا كما يقال هذا صغير في جنب ذلك الماضي

THALABI:v8p246/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v8p246/r7.claim: An alternative takes it as God's path and religion; Arabic calls a means or path to something its side, as a poet says he endured bitterness for your sake.
THALABI:v8p246/r7.anchor: وقيل: في سبيل الله ودينه. والعرب تسمي السبب والطريق الى الشيء جنبا

THALABI:v8p246/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p246/r8.claim: The phrase can mean the side leading to God's pleasure and reward; Arabic also uses junb for a side, as a poet contrasts people on one side and the prince on another.
THALABI:v8p246/r8.anchor: وقال في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضى الله تعالى وثوابه، والعرب تسمي الجانب جنبا.

THALABI:v8p246/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r9.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v8p246/r9.claim: The cited line الناس جنب والأمير جنب demonstrates junb meaning a side, with people on one side and the ruler on the other.
THALABI:v8p246/r9.anchor: قال الشاعر: الناس جنب والأمير جنب

THALABI:v8p246/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p246/r10.claim: The regretful speaker admits mocking God's religion, Book, Messenger, and believers.
THALABI:v8p246/r10.anchor: المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه ورسوله والمؤمنين.

THALABI:v8p246/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r11.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p246/r11.claim: Qatada says the person not only neglected God's obedience but went further and mocked those who obeyed Him.
THALABI:v8p246/r11.anchor: قال قتادة: في هذه الآية لم يكفه ان ضيع طاعة الله تعالى

THALABI:v8p246/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p246/r12.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v8p246/r12.claim: Abu Salih tells of an Israelite scholar who abandoned learning for vice after Satan promised him a long life and later repentance; dying in sin, he regretted spending life obeying Satan, and God revealed his story. No grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p246/r12.anchor: عن أبي صالح: (يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r6.claim: The regret is for having neglected obedience to God and following His way.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r6.anchor: أي: قصرت في طاعة الله، وسلوك طريقة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r7.claim: The speaker admits to having mocked God's religion and Book.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:53-56/r7.anchor: ما كنت إلا من المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه

ELMALILI:39:56-63/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r1.claim: A soul will lament its failures toward God and admit that it had been among those who mocked.
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r1.anchor: Eyvah, Allah yanında yaptığım eksikliklerden dolayı hasretime bak, doğrusu ben eğlenenlerden idim

ELMALILI:39:56-63/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r2.claim: The phrase “that a soul should say” means “lest a soul say,” expressing the aim of preventing this regretful speech.
ELMALILI:39:56-63/r2.anchor: Bir nefis diyeceği için[^1] yani dememek için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r1.claim: The verse vividly presents the deep remorse, admissions, complaints, and futile wishes of people who wasted their worldly chance to submit and follow God’s rulings, rejecting or opposing Islam and living in unbelief and sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r1.anchor: Burada, dünyada fırsat eldeyken Allah’a yönelip O’na teslim olmaları ve O’nun “en güzel hükümler”ine uymaları gerektiği halde bu fırsatı kaçıranların

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r2.claim: The authors prefer Ibn Ashur’s reading of tafrīṭ as failing to do what was required; the various interpretations converge on this sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r2.anchor: bu yorumların sonucu İbn Âşûr’un verdiği (XXIV, 46), bizim de tercih ettiğimiz anlama varmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r3.claim: The authors prefer Zemakhshari and Shawkani’s interpretation of janb Allāh as obedience to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r3.anchor: bizim tercihimiz Zemahşerî (III, 352) ve Şevkânî’nin (IV, 539) yorumuna dayanmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r4.claim: Tabari transmits reports explaining janb Allāh as God’s command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:56/r4.anchor: Taberî’nin aktardığı bazı rivayetlerde bu deyim “Allah’ın emri” şeklinde de açıklanmıştır

BURHAN:v3p352/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r1.speaker: النووي
BURHAN:v3p352/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi explains that hadith prohibitions phrased as statements (‘he does not propose’ or ‘bid’) are more forceful because a prophetic report cannot fail, whereas a prohibition can be disobeyed; ‘do not ask’ may be read indicatively or as a direct prohibition.
BURHAN:v3p352/r1.anchor: وقال النووي في شرح مسلم في باب تحريم الجمع بين المرأة وعمتها وخالتها وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يخطب الرجل على خطبة أخيه ولا يسوم على سوم أخيه هكذا هو في جميع النسخ

BURHAN:v3p352/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r2.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v3p352/r2.claim: Al-Farra says the vocative means ‘what a regret’; حسرة is the most intense remorse, since the heart remains exhausted.
BURHAN:v3p352/r2.anchor: قال الفراء معناه فيالها من حسرة والحسرة في اللغة أشد الندم لأن القلب يبقى حسيرا

BURHAN:v3p352/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r3.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v3p352/r3.claim: The Basrans call this one of the Qur’an’s hardest constructions because regret is not normally addressed; the vocative instead conveys astonishment and alerts the listener, like ‘O wonder!’
BURHAN:v3p352/r3.anchor: عن البصريين أن هذه من أصعب مسألة في القرآن لأن الحسرة لا تنادي وإنما تنادى الاشخاص لأن فائدته التنبيه

BURHAN:v3p352/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p352/r4.claim: The implied ‘O regret, be present’ is stronger than simply saying ‘astonishing’; the vocative puts the exclamation directly before the listener.
BURHAN:v3p352/r4.anchor: ولكن المعنى على التعجب كقوله يا عجبا لم فعلت

BURHAN:v3p352/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r6.speaker: قوم
BURHAN:v3p352/r6.claim: Some grammarians derive يا حسرتى from يا حسرتاه, with the final hāʾ dropped for ease; the reading يا أسفى على يوسف is a parallel.
BURHAN:v3p352/r6.anchor: ومنهم قال الأصل يا حسرتاه ثم اسقطوا الهاء تخفيفا ولهذا قرأ عاصم ﴿ يا أسفى على يوسف ﴾

BURHAN:v3p352/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p352/r7.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v3p352/r7.claim: Ibn Jinni says the wording means that, if regret could truly be called, this would be the moment to call it.
BURHAN:v3p352/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جنى في كتاب الفسر معناه أنه لو كانت الحسرة مما يصح نداؤه لكان هذا وقتها

BURHAN:v1p468/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p468/r1.claim: The reader should separate each sura from the previous by pausing or saying the basmala, and not begin another sura before finishing the first.
BURHAN:v1p468/r1.anchor: وأن يفصل كل سورة عما قبلها إما بالوقف أو التسمية ولا يقرأ من أخرى قبل الفراغ من الأولى

BURHAN:v1p468/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468/r2.speaker: البيهقي
BURHAN:v1p468/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi cites the Prophet’s practice of pausing at each verse, even when the syntax is incomplete, and prefers following this Sunnah to reciters’ pursuit of thematic purposes.
BURHAN:v1p468/r2.anchor: وقال البيهقى رحمه الله وقد ذكر حديث كان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يقطع قراءته آية آية ومتابعة السنة أولى فيما ذهب إليه أهل العلم بالقراءات

BURHAN:v1p468/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p468/r3.claim: The reader should be grateful for the gift of memorizing the Book, value it above worldly possessions, and avoid boasting or pursuing worldly gain through recitation.
BURHAN:v1p468/r3.anchor: ومنها أن يعتقد جزيل ما أنعم الله عليه إذ أهله لحفظ كتابه

BURHAN:v1p468/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468/r4.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p468/r4.claim: Al-Halimi advises against reciting in markets and extends the restriction to bathhouses; al-Nawawi permits quiet recitation on the road when there is no idle talk.
BURHAN:v1p468/r4.anchor: وليتجنب القراءة فى الأسواق قاله الحليمى وألحق به الحمام وقال النووى لا بأس به فى الطريق سرا حيث لا لغو فيها

BURHAN:v1p468/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p468/r5.claim: A Qur’an reader should avoid dirty places and sin, maintain composure and self-accountability, and embody the Qur’an’s promises and warnings in character.
BURHAN:v1p468/r5.anchor: وألا يقرأ فى المواضع القذرة وأن يكون ذا سكينة ووقار مجانبا للذنب محاسبا نفسه يعرف القرآن فى سمته وخلقه

ITQAN:v3p14/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p14/r1.speaker: ابن الصلاح
ITQAN:v3p14/r1.claim: Ibn al-Salah says the method under discussion was followed by the early community and chosen by leading jurists and hadith authorities; the excerpt does not restate the method's name.
ITQAN:v3p14/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الصلاح على هذه الطريقة مضى صدر الأمة وساداتها وإياها اختار أئمة الفقهاء وقاداتها وإليها دعا أئمة الحديث

ITQAN:v3p14/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p14/r2.speaker: ابن برهان
ITQAN:v3p14/r2.claim: Ibn Burhan chose interpretation; he locates the dispute in whether the Qur'an may contain meanings unknown to us or whether the firmly grounded scholars know them.
ITQAN:v3p14/r2.anchor: واختار ابن برهان مذهب التأويل قال ومنشأ الخلاف بين الفريقين هل يجوز أن يكون في القرآن شيء لم نعلم معناه أو لا بل يعلمه الراسخون في العلم

ITQAN:v3p14/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p14/r3.speaker: ابن دقيق العيد
ITQAN:v3p14/r3.claim: Ibn Daqiq al-Id takes a middle path: interpretation close to Arabic is acceptable; when remote, one suspends judgment while affirming the intended meaning with transcendence.
ITQAN:v3p14/r3.anchor: وتوسط ابن دقيق العيد فقال إذا كان التأويل قريبا من لسان العرب لم ينكر أو بعيدا توقفنا عنه وآمنا بمعناه على الوجه الذي أريد به مع التنزيه

ITQAN:v3p14/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p14/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p14/r4.claim: Applying the apparent Arabic meaning, the author takes جنب الله in 39:56 as God's right and what is due to Him.
ITQAN:v3p14/r4.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله ﴾ فنحمله على حق الله وما يجب له

ITQAN:v3p248#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p248#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p248#3/r1.claim: The chapter on self-reproach gives the regretful soul's cry in 39:56 as an example, alongside the wrongdoer biting his hands and wishing he had followed the Messenger.
ITQAN:v3p248#3/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أن تقول نفس يا حسرتى على ما فرطت في جنب الله ﴾ الآيات

ITQAN:v4p456#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r1.claim: Early Qur'anic notation used dots for short vowels: fatḥa above the first letter, ḍamma at the end, and kasra below the first; al-Dani followed it.
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r1.anchor: كان الشكل في الصدر الأول نقطا فالفتحة نقطة على أول الحرف والضمة على آخره والكسرة تحت أوله وعليه مشى الداني

ITQAN:v4p456#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r2.claim: The current vowel signs, devised by al-Khalil and clearer and more widely used, derive from letters: a long mark for fatḥa, the same below for kasra, and a small wāw above for ḍamma.
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r2.anchor: والذي اشتهر الآن الضبط بالحركات المأخوذة من الحروف وهو الذي أخرجه الخليل وهو أكثر وأوضح وعليه العمل فالفتح شكلة مستطيلة فوق الحرف والكسر كذلك تحته والضم واو ضغرى فوقه

ITQAN:v4p456#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r3.claim: Tanwin marks are doubled; omitted alif and hamza are written in red, and the iqlab sign is a red mīm above nūn or tanwin before bāʾ.
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r3.anchor: والتنوين زيادة مثلها فإن كان مظهرا وذلك قبل حرف حلق ركبت فوقها وإلا تابعت بينهما وتكتب الألف المحذوفة والمبدل منها في محلها حمراء والهمزة المحذوفة

ITQAN:v4p456#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r4.claim: The notation also marks assimilation and concealment, leaves assimilated letters bare and doubles the following letter, except ṭāʾ before tāʾ, marked with sukūn as in فرطت; the elongation mark must not exceed the madd.
ITQAN:v4p456#2/r4.anchor: وقبل الحلق سكون وتقرأ عند الإدغام والإخفاء ويسكن كل مسكن ويعرى المدغم ويشدد ما بعده إلا الطاء قبل التاء فيكتب عليها السكون

ITQAN:v2p329/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p329/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p329/r2.claim: The phrase لمن الساخرين is glossed as the foolish or senile ones.

ITQAN:v1p29/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p29/r1.claim: The author organizes Qur'anic studies into eighty kinds by combining topics; separating what he merged would yield more than three hundred, and most kinds already have monographs.
ITQAN:v1p29/r1.anchor: فهذه ثمانون نوعا على سبيل الإدماج ولو نوعت باعتبار ما أدمجته في ضمنها لزادت على الثلاثمائة وغالب هذه الأنواع فيها تصانيف مفردة

ITQAN:v1p29/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p29/r2.claim: He lists earlier works on Qur'anic studies by Ibn al-Jawzi, al-Sakhawi, Abu Shama, and Shidhila, judging each a tiny sample compared with his book.
ITQAN:v1p29/r2.anchor: فنون الأفنان في علوم القرآن لابن الجوزي وجمال القراء للشيخ علم الدين السخاوي والمرشد الوجيز في علوم تتعلق بالقرآن العزيز لأبي شامة

NAHHAS:v4p17/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p17/r4.claim: أن تقول is accusative with the sense كراهة أن تقول; the Kufians explain it as لئلا تقول.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r4.anchor: في موضع نصب أي كراهة أن تقول وعند الكوفيين بمعنى لئلا تقول نفس

NAHHAS:v4p17/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p17/r5.claim: The original is يا حسرتي; yā becomes alif for ease, and calling regret conveys its abiding presence more forcefully than merely reporting it.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r5.anchor: والأصل يا حسرتي أي يا ندمي فأبدل من الياء ألفا لأنها أخف فالفائدة في نداء الحسرة

NAHHAS:v4p17/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p17/r6.claim: Al-Farra permits يا حسرتاه in connected speech like a lamentation, but al-Nahhas rejects it: grammarians call it wrong, this is not a lament, and the written text and readings lack hāʾ.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r6.anchor: وأجاز الفراء في الوصل يا حسرتاه على كذا ويا حسرتاه على كذا

NAHHAS:v4p17/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r7.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v4p17/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses God's side as remembrance of God, meaning the Quran and acting upon it.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r7.anchor: قال الضحاك أي في ذكر الله قال يعني القرآن والعمل به

NAHHAS:v4p17/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
NAHHAS:v4p17/r8.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says any sitting, walking, or lying down without remembering God becomes a regret on Judgment Day.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r8.anchor: وفي حديث ابن عجلان عن سعيد المقبري عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما جلس رجل مجلسا

NAHHAS:v4p17/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r9.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
NAHHAS:v4p17/r9.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi describes regrets including seeing one's former wealth benefiting another in the scales and seeing others granted sight or higher rank while oneself is deprived.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r9.anchor: قال إبراهيم التيمي من الحسرات يوم القيامة أن يرى الرجل ماله الذي آتاه الله إياه يوم القيامة في ميزان غيره

NAHHAS:v4p17/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p17/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v4p17/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the phrase as: I was only one of the mockers.
NAHHAS:v4p17/r10.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي ما كنت إلا من المستهزئين

BAQILLANI:v1p281/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r7.claim: The imagined cry of regret is the ultimate warning against neglecting one’s duty toward God.
BAQILLANI:v1p281/r7.anchor: وهذا نهاية في التحذير من التفريط

BURHAN:v3p180/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.claim: The vocative often drops the yāʾ attached to the first-person pronoun because calling favors omission; Qur'anic forms also retain it with sukūn or fatḥa, or replace it with alif.
BURHAN:v3p180/r1.anchor: باب حذف ألا ترى أنه يحذف منه التنوين وبعض الاسم

BURHAN:v3p96/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p96/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v3p96/r3.claim: The Kufans explain an before a future verb as لئلا, “lest,” in examples such as أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر.
BURHAN:v3p96/r3.anchor: أحدهما للكوفيين أن المعنى لئلا يقولوا ولئلا تقول نفس

BURHAN:v3p96/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p96/r4.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v3p96/r4.claim: The Basrans instead posit an omitted verbal noun or object, such as كراهة or حذار, before the clause.
BURHAN:v3p96/r4.anchor: الثاني للبصريين أن المفعول محذوف أي كراهة أن يقولوا أو حذار أن يقولوا

BURHAN:v4p227/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p227/r8.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v4p227/r8.claim: In purpose clauses such as يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا, the Basrans supply an omitted noun, كراهة, before أن; the sense is “lest you go astray.”
BURHAN:v4p227/r8.anchor: وقال البصريون على حذف مضاف أي كراهة أن تضلوا

BURHAN:v2p84/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p84/r2.speaker: اللغويون
BURHAN:v2p84/r2.claim: The language scholars gloss ‘in God’s side’ as ‘in obedience to and command of God’: neglect cannot occur in a bodily side, so the phrase should not be taken as attributing limbs to God.
BURHAN:v2p84/r2.anchor: قال اللغويون معناه ما فرطت في طاعة الله وأمره لأن التفريط لا يقع إلا في ذلك

BURHAN:v3p228/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p228/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p228/r4.claim: The regretful cry is the strongest warning against neglect.
BURHAN:v3p228/r4.anchor: وهذا أشد ما يكون من التحذير من التفريط

ITQAN:v3p19/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r2.claim: Here جنب الله means God’s obedience and due right, since neglect applies to these rather than to a literal side.
ITQAN:v3p19/r2.anchor: أي في طاعته وحقه لأن التفريط إنما يقع في ذلك ولا يقع في الجنب المعهود

RUMMANI:v1p108/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p108/r5.claim: The soul's cry of regret over neglecting its duty toward God is the strongest warning against falling short.
RUMMANI:v1p108/r5.anchor: {أن تقول نفس ياحسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله}

DAMGHANI:v1p232/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p232/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p232/r3.claim: Sākhir means one who mocks; the source groups verses about mockery under this sense.
DAMGHANI:v1p232/r3.anchor: يعني المستهزئين مثلها في سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r11.claim: Janb Allāh can mean obedience to God.
